doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Influences: Armstrong, Roy Eldridge and Dizzy Gillespie
summary: Young names Armstrong and Eldridge as influences and recalls hanging with Dizzy Gillespie in New York when Gillespie was with Cab Calloway.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: So you stated earlier that your influences were Louis Armstrong. Louis Armstrong was a major influence when you were first learning to play trumpet.
Then Roy Eldridge was another influence. Who were some other people you were listening to you felt influenced your sound?
Dizzy Gillespie. [laughs] Me and Dizzy was good friends.
So you met him? When did you meet Dizzy?

When did I meet Dizzy…how did I meet Dizzy. I met Dizzy, Dizzy and I did a lot of thing together. When I come to, I was in New York and Dizzy took a likening to me before he got to be Dizzy, I mean before he got the name. He had the name, but he wasn‘t Dizzy Gillespie yet. You know what I‘m saying? He hadn‘t made those things that made him Dizzy yet. And I used to run with Dizzy before he got to be Dizzy.
When he was still with Cab‘s band?

Young:…when he was with Cab‘s band. See I was with Jimmie Lunceford, and he was with Cab‘s band and we used to kind of hang together and everything…and it was other trumpet players I used to be hanging with. I wish I could call their names, man, they were good trumpet players in them big bands, you know them, too. I can‘t think of nobody‘s name.
